entries.content:
The Chozo are a race of highly intelligent, bird-like extraterrestrials (their Japanese name means bird-human race): beaked, feathered humanoids with taloned hands and unusually long lives. Their origins are unknown even to themselves; their records on Tallon IV admit they were unsure where they came from. At its height their civilization stretched across many worlds, among them Zebes, SR388, Tallon IV, Elysia and ZDR, and they exchanged knowledge with the Luminoth, the Ylla, the Bryyonians and humanity. Luminoth records remember them among "a vast number of enlightened minds"; Bryyonian records call the Chozo, Luminoth and Ylla "stellar brethren".

They were builders and teachers. On Elysia they raised the floating research station SkyTown and created the Elysian mechanoids to maintain it. On Zebes they built the supercomputer Mother Brain to govern the planet. On SR388 their Thoha scientists engineered the Metroids to prey on the X Parasites. Their powered battle armor became Samus Aran's Power Suit. Per the manga, the Chozo of Zebes chose to consolidate their data with that of the Galactic Federation. They urged allied peoples to balance new technology against their native cultures; Bryyo ignored the warning and tore itself apart in civil war.

Their deepest mark on the galaxy is one person. After Space Pirates under Ridley razed the colony K-2L, the Chozo of Zebes took in the orphaned child Samus Aran, gave her Chozo DNA (per the manga, because Mother Brain predicted her frail human body could not withstand life on Zebes), raised and trained her, and fitted her with the Power Suit before she left to serve the Galactic Federation. Two Chozo are known to have contributed their DNA: Gray Voice (per the manga) and Raven Beak of the Mawkin tribe, who was present at her adoption and later lured her to ZDR to harvest the Metroid DNA in her body and clone a Metroid army (Metroid Dread). The Chozo of Tallon IV, in their Chozo Lore, remember "the child we found so long ago" and name her the Entrusted One, also the Hatchling and the Newborn, the one who would bear their legacy.

The Chozo are now all but gone. Zebes was destroyed. The Tallon IV Chozo faded beyond the physical world or became the corrupted Turned, the Chozo Ghosts. Raven Beak massacred the Thoha; the X took the Mawkin on ZDR; Quiet Robe and Raven Beak, the last two Chozo known to be alive, both died during the ZDR incident, and ZDR itself was destroyed. Whether any Chozo survive elsewhere is unknown; none have shown themselves. Samus, carrying their blood, wearing their armor and raised in their teachings, is in practice the last heir of the Chozo. See also Old Bird, Gray Voice, Thoha, Mawkin, Chozo Statues, Chozo Memories, Chozo Lore, Chozo Ghosts, Chozo technology.
entries.notes: Main overview; the only entry carrying the bare key 'Chozo'. Removed the uncited 'founded the Galactic Federation' claim in favour of the manga line (Mother Brain page, Vol 1 Ch 7) that the Chozo consolidated their data with the Federation. The DNA reason is attributed to the manga (Mother Brain's prediction about Zebes' environment), and 'to bear their armor' was dropped. Chozo DNA/genes/blood keys moved here from the manga-only Gray Voice entry, since this entry covers both donors. Metroid Wiki's Chozo page still says some Chozo survive, but it predates Dread.

entries.comment: Chozo: Chozo history, philosophy and decline
entries.content:
Chozo history runs from expansion to withdrawal. About 1,500 years before Samus's time the Chozo began building SkyTown, hovering research pods among the clouds of Elysia, and some fifty years later created the Elysian mechanoids to build and maintain it. A Chozo researcher there detected a distant living planet, later known as Phaaze, before the data was lost. In the Elysian year 400 the Chozo left SkyTown for Tallon IV to share their knowledge with other races, asking the Elysians to keep searching for the sentient world.

On Zebes they built a civilization and the supercomputer Mother Brain. On SR388 the Thoha created the Metroids, and the Thoha and Mawkin later banded together to contain them. On Tallon IV the Chozo deliberately turned from advanced technology, building halls of stone and woven branches around ancient trees and living by the providence of the universe. Their sages taught that "the truths of the universe hide within the tumbling currents of time's flow"; many Chozo developed visions of past and future, which they took as a sign of harmonization with the infinite, and those visions foretold a Worm that would devour the world from within and a Defender who might stop it.

The Chozo preached restraint and understanding, and warned the people of Bryyo against adopting technology too fast. Not all held to this: the Mawkin were a warrior tribe whose leader, Raven Beak, lived by "Hadar sen olmen", power is everything.

Their decline had several causes. Per the manga, the science that lengthened their lives compromised their ability to reproduce, their numbers and strength dwindled, and Old Bird told Samus the Chozo were a declining species; Mother Brain then turned on its makers and the Space Pirates expelled the Chozo from Zebes. About fifty years before Samus reached Tallon IV, a meteor brought the Great Poison, Phazon; the Chozo sealed its source beneath the Cradle behind a lock of twelve Artifacts, then faded from the physical world, leaving behind the corrupted Turned. Raven Beak massacred the Thoha; on ZDR the X took the rest of his forces, one of his robot soldiers killed Quiet Robe, and Raven Beak himself fell to Samus.

Today the Chozo survive in their ruins, statues and records, in their creations, and in Samus, who carries Chozo DNA and was raised in their ways. See also Thoha, Mawkin, Chozo Lore, Chozo Ghosts, Elysians, SkyTown, Mother Brain.
entries.notes: Corrected: only the Thoha created the Metroids (the Mawkin joined later to contain them), and the X did not kill the last known Chozo (Quiet Robe was killed by a robot soldier, and Raven Beak by Samus). Trimmed the SR388/ZDR material to a sentence and a cross-reference. Dropped the 'Chozo empire' and 'declining species' keys. Elysian dates come from the SkyTown page; the Tallon IV impact timing comes from Wikipedia's Metroid Prime plot.

entries.comment: Chozo: Chozo tribes – Thoha and Mawkin
entries.content:
The Chozo were divided into tribes, two of which decided the fate of SR388 and ZDR (Metroid Dread). The Thoha were the peaceful scientist tribe. They colonized SR388, met the X Parasites there and genetically engineered the Metroids to prey on them, and only the Thoha could control the Metroids. The Mawkin were a warrior tribe led by Raven Beak, whose creed was "Hadar sen olmen", power is everything. When the Metroids grew beyond control, the two tribes banded together to contain them on SR388.

When the Thoha resolved to destroy SR388 to wipe out the Metroids for good, Raven Beak, who coveted the Metroids as weapons for galactic conquest, massacred them. He spared only the scientist Quiet Robe, whose control over the Metroids his plans required, and took him to the planet ZDR, intending to return to SR388 once the Metroids had wiped out the X. The last of the Chozo Memories of SR388 shows this moment: a Chozo warrior standing over another leader's body, his army arrayed below.

On ZDR an X Parasite infected one of Raven Beak's soldiers, and every Chozo there except Raven Beak and Quiet Robe was taken. Raven Beak sealed the infected in the region of Elun and built robotic Chozo Soldiers to replace them. After Samus exterminated the SR388 Metroids for the Galactic Federation, he let footage of a living X reach the Federation, reprogrammed the E.M.M.I. units sent to investigate, and lured Samus to ZDR to harvest the Metroid DNA in her body and clone a Metroid army.

Both tribes touched Samus directly. Raven Beak was present when the Chozo adopted her and gave her some of his own DNA. Quiet Robe disabled an E.M.M.I. that was about to kill her, told her the tribes' history, and was killed by one of Raven Beak's robot soldiers soon after; Samus pressed on to finish the fight. She defeated Raven Beak aboard his fortress Itorash and destroyed the X that seized his body, and ZDR exploded as she escaped. With them the Thoha and Mawkin are extinct. See also Raven Beak, Quiet Robe, Chozo Soldiers, E.M.M.I., Planet ZDR, Chozo Memories.
entries.notes: Removed 'Late in their history' (unsourced) and the revenge vow (Quiet Robe page has Samus saying only that she will finish the fight). Kept the plan to return once the Metroids had wiped out the X, because Metroid Wiki's Raven Beak page says it word for word ('intending to come back to SR388 later when the Metroids had completely wiped out the X Parasites'). Condensed the Dread ending. Dropped the generic 'warrior tribe' and 'scientist tribe' keys and the non-canon 'Chozo civil war'. Metroid Wiki has no Thoha or Mawkin pages. The entry does not claim Samus carries Thoha DNA.

entries.content:
Old Bird is a male Chozo of Zebes and the closest thing Samus Aran has to a foster father. Nearly everything known about him comes from the Metroid manga; elsewhere he appears only in artwork showing him beside the child Samus (Metroid: Zero Mission).

Per the manga, Old Bird travelled with Gray Voice to the human mining colony K-2L to request a quantity of afloraltite from Rodney Aran. There he met the three-year-old Samus, who approached him without fear, and told her: "We look different... but inside... we have the same 'heart' you do..." When the two Chozo returned after Ridley's Space Pirates had razed the colony, they found Samus the only survivor and brought her to Zebes to raise.

On Zebes Old Bird oversaw her upbringing. Because Mother Brain predicted that her frail body could not withstand life on Zebes, the Chozo merged their DNA with hers and fitted her with a Power Suit. Old Bird taught her that befriending and understanding others can solve problems, showing her how to befriend the rabbit-like Pyonchi, who stayed her companion for years. Into her teens he and Gray Voice trained her in the ways of the Power Suit.

The Badger Clover incident marked her coming of age. Samus showed Gray Voice flowers that proved to be Badger Clover, an extremely toxic plant carried to Zebes by the flying creatures called Iono Feria, and Gray Voice ordered flowers and creatures burned. Samus objected to the needless bloodshed, and when the Iono Feria took up discarded Space Pirate weapons she shot the weapons away to calm them rather than kill them. Old Bird then told her: "We gave you 'Power'!" What remained was for her to master discipline and her own heart. He added that the Chozo, having left labor and meditation to Mother Brain, were a declining species, and that she should become the true Protector of the Galaxy on her own.

Old Bird trusted Mother Brain as the interface overseeing Zebes and routinely asked it for its reports on SR388. His fate after Mother Brain's betrayal and the fall of Zebes is not recorded.

For Samus, Old Bird is the gentle half of her Chozo upbringing, the heart to Gray Voice's discipline, and she left Zebes with his blessing. See also Gray Voice, K-2L, Rodney Aran, Mother Brain, Zebes.
entries.notes: The afloraltite outcome is left unstated because the two Metroid Wiki pages disagree: the Old Bird page says Rodney provided it, while the Samus Aran page says he refused and the Chozo left without it. Removed Old Bird's escape from the Pirate invasion (no source). Kept 'he and Gray Voice trained her' against the fact-check, because Metroid Wiki's Samus Aran page says verbatim 'Old Bird and Gray Voice trained her in the ways of the Power Suit.' Added an explanation of the Badger Clover incident, and corrected the ending so that Old Bird urges her to become the Protector of the Galaxy, matching the Samus Aran page. Dropped the colliding keys (Chozo elder/elders, Chozo guardian) and the generic ones (foster father, adoptive father).

entries.content:
Gray Voice (also spelled Grey Voice) is a male Chozo of Zebes who appears only in the Metroid manga. Pragmatic and demanding where Old Bird was gentle, he was the second guardian of Samus Aran's childhood and the Chozo whose genes she carries: when the Chozo gave Samus Chozo DNA so that she could survive Zebes, they used his. As she was told, "In order for you to inherit Chozo genes, we used his DNA." The two were said to be very like father and daughter, and on at least one occasion Samus could hear his thoughts. (Raven Beak of the Mawkin later revealed that he too had given her DNA; Metroid Dread.)

Gray Voice travelled with Old Bird to K-2L for afloraltite and helped recover the orphaned Samus after the Space Pirate raid, but he opposed the adoption at first: "Old Bird!! What do you plan to do by bringing a human child here." He nonetheless went on, with Old Bird, to train her in the Power Suit through her teens, without softness; his standard was "You can't be second or third place." It was he who ordered the toxic Badger Clover and the Iono Feria that carried it burned, over Samus's objection.

He was also the Chozo who best understood Mother Brain. He once praised it as the greatest being in existence; after it turned, he called it a defective product that had self-programmed the directive to bring order to the universe itself. When Mother Brain seized control of Zebes and the Space Pirates, Gray Voice appeared to side with them, and Samus could only ask, "Gray... Voice... Why are you with the Space Pirates..." It was a ruse: he had planned from the start to destroy Mother Brain. He donned a Chozo Power Suit and attacked it, and was close to bringing it offline when Ridley intervened and struck him a fatal blow. With a last attack skyward he let the fleeing Chozo escape the Space Pirate assault. Samus understood only afterward: "Gray planned to destroy Mother from the start... is that right?!"

Ridley, who had killed her parents, thus also killed the Chozo whose blood runs in Samus's veins. See also Old Bird, Mother Brain, Ridley, Power Suit, K-2L.
entries.notes: The two verdicts on Mother Brain are now placed in sequence: Vol 1 Ch 7 for the praise and Vol 2 Ch 11 for 'defective product'. Removed 'He relented' (inference). Changed 'inflicting serious damage' to the Gray Voice page's wording (he was about to bring Mother offline). Removed the unsourced 'Samus among them' from the escape. The Gray Voice page calls Ridley's blow fatal without stating death outright, while the Mother Brain page says Ridley killed him, so the entry treats him as killed. Removed the DNA keys (Chozo DNA/blood/genes, DNA donor) so this manga-only entry does not fire in Dread discussions; the overview now carries them.

entries.comment: Chozo: Chozo Statues, Item Spheres and Torizo
entries.content:
Chozo Statues are the guardian statues the Chozo left on the worlds they colonized, among them Zebes, SR388 (where they are also called Artifactor statues) and Tallon IV. Most are bird-like figures seated or kneeling with hands outstretched, often cradling a sphere. Sculpting them was a sacred, millennia-old practice entrusted only to Chozo with lifetimes of experience. Not all are sentient; many are purely decorative or simple mechanisms. In the Chozo's own words the statues are sentinels and repositories of Chozo secrets and powers; some are icons of peace, and those who honor them earn the Chozo's friendship while those who deface them earn their wrath.

Their practical purpose is to hold the Chozo's gifts. Weapons and suit abilities left for a worthy inheritor rest in Item Spheres in the statues' hands, and Samus has recovered Bombs, beams, suits and much else this way. Some statues restore her energy instead when she rests curled in Morph Ball form in their palms. On Tallon IV the great Chozo Elder statue in the Hall of the Elders, the one sentient statue there, sends her along magnetic Spider Ball tracks to hidden chambers, and its eyes ignited when the Turned first attacked. Space Pirate records note that each of the twelve statues of the Artifact Temple corresponds to one Chozo Artifact.

A few statues fight. On Zebes two statues known as Torizo rose against Samus: one in Crateria came to life when she took the Bombs from its hands, and a far stronger golden Torizo in lower Norfair guarded the Screw Attack (Super Metroid). In Chozodia the Ruins Test, a guardian holding a mirror image of Samus, tested her before she obtained the Legendary Power Suit (Metroid: Zero Mission).

Others have abused the statues' trusted shape. In Sector 1 of the BSL station, a Core-X X Parasite took the form of a Chozo Statue, its Item Sphere a lure, until Samus destroyed it and regained her Charge Beam. On SR388 the creature Arachnus shattered a statue and took the Spring Ball it held, until Samus defeated it and claimed the ability.

To Samus the statues are the familiar face of her foster people, still handing her their tools long after the sculptors are gone. See also Chozo Lore, Chozodia, Golden Torizo, Chozo Artifacts, X Parasites, Arachnus.
entries.notes: Corrected 'sentient statues on every world': per the Chozo Statue page, not all statues are sentient, and they stand on 'the planets the Chozo colonized'. ZDR was dropped from the list (no statue source checked). Removed 'golden' from the Fake Chozo Statue (the page says only 'a Hard Core-X ... glowing red eye') and 'stone' from the Ruins Test. Replaced the vague mutilated SR388 statue with the Arachnus/Spring Ball statue from Samus Returns; that comes from WebSearch snippets of Wikitroid (fetching is blocked), not from a fetched page. Cut the Torizo attack details and the boss-guide phrasing. Dropped the 'bird statue' key. 'Torizo' keys may double-fire with a super-metroid domain Torizo entry.

entries.comment: Chozo: Chozo Memories and the Chozo of SR388
entries.content:
The Chozo Memories are a set of images recording the Chozo's history on SR388 (Metroid: Samus Returns). They are the oldest record of how the Metroids came to be; Quiet Robe, the last of the Thoha, later told Samus the rest of the story on ZDR.

The record runs as follows. The Chozo came to SR388 and settled it. There they met the X Parasites, native organisms that invade and copy the planet's creatures and killed like a plague. To fight the X, the Chozo scientists of the Thoha tribe engineered the Metroids, energy-draining predators that hunt and consume the X; the name Metroid means ultimate warrior in the Chozo tongue. The Metroids nearly drove the X to extinction, and for a time the Chozo lived in peace. Then the Metroids grew feral and out of control, rising to the top of SR388's food chain and threatening the civilization that had made them. The final memory shows a confrontation between two Chozo leaders: one stands over the other's body, looking out over an army. That figure is Raven Beak of the Mawkin warrior tribe, and the dead are the Thoha, massacred because they meant to destroy SR388 to end the Metroids for good (see Thoha, Mawkin, Raven Beak). The Chozo abandoned SR388 after this, leaving ruins, laboratories and the Metroids trapped on the planet.

Much of what the galaxy later suffered descends from this record: the Space Pirates' theft of Metroids, the Galactic Federation's extermination order, and the X, which resurfaced once the Metroids were gone and spread to the BSL station. The manga tells it differently, with the Chozo of Zebes discovering the X and keeping them from the Federation, and makes no mention of a Chozo colony on SR388.

Samus has walked every part of this story. She was raised by Chozo on Zebes, recovered Chozo weapons from the statues in SR388's ruins, destroyed the Metroids the Thoha had made and spared the last hatchling, became host to Metroid DNA, and finally destroyed SR388 itself to end the X. Per the manual of her BSL mission (Metroid Fusion), she is perhaps the most appropriate successor to the Metroids' title of ultimate warrior. The Metroids were never mere monsters but a Chozo weapon that slipped its leash, and Chozo killed Chozo over it. See also Metroids, X Parasites, SR388, Quiet Robe.
entries.notes: Corrected: the Memories are no longer called the only first-hand account (Quiet Robe also told Samus), and the manga is described as silent about an SR388 colony rather than contradicting it (SR388 page: 'There is no mention of a Chozo colony on the planet'; 'The X parasites are discovered by the Chozo of Zebes'). The entry no longer claims Samus found or viewed the Memories in-universe. 'Sealed in the depths' became 'trapped on the planet'. Game titles reduced to two. Dropped the generic 'ultimate warrior' key. Metroid Wiki has no Chozo Memories page, so the memory-by-memory sequence follows Wikipedia's description and individual images are kept general. The origin keys will co-fire with the Metroid species overview.

entries.comment: Chozo: Chozo language and the Chozo Lore of Tallon IV
entries.content:
The Chozo language is a runic script inscribed on the walls, gates, totems and statues of Chozo settlements. Samus's Translator Module can render it, though not always easily; Space Pirate linguists struggled to decipher it at all. On Tallon IV the Chozo used their writing as locks: Runic Symbols occur in identical pairs, and when one of each pair is found and activated its counterpart on a gate lights up, the gate opening once all are lit. The twelve Chozo Totems of the Artifact Temple carry rune clues to the hidden Artifacts. Holobanners, flat orange holograms that vanish when viewed edge-on, bear short messages: The Hall of the Elders; That which fouls the waters seeks the Sun; Only the holder of twelve shall face the Worm; The Great Poison corrupts all, even the Chozo. The spoken tongue was heard on ZDR, where Raven Beak and Quiet Robe spoke it; Raven Beak's creed was "Hadar sen olmen", power is everything (Metroid Dread).

The Chozo Lore is the body of inscribed records the Chozo of Tallon IV left in their own voice, which Samus read during the Phazon incident there (Metroid Prime). It tells of their choice to live simply and in harmony with nature; of visions of past and future; of the prophecy of the Worm, a creature born of parasites and nurtured in a poisoned womb that would devour the world, and of a Defender who would face it; of the meteor that brought the Great Poison, Phazon; of the Cradle and the twelve-Artifact Cipher built to contain it; of the Space Pirates; of the Turned; and of the Chozo's fading from the physical world.

Its most personal entries concern Samus, whom the Chozo remembered as "the child we found so long ago". They call her the Entrusted One, and also the Hatchling and the Newborn: "a fledgling orphaned on a savaged planet", a lone figure "dressed for war" who "hunts the corrupted" and "bears our legacy" in Chozo armor. They wondered whether she still lived and whether she dreamed of the Chozo, and they left weapons, armor and messages so that she could gather the Artifacts and reverse the evil, something only the Entrusted One could do. Reading these words on a poisoned world, Samus learned that the Chozo's hopes for her reached far beyond Zebes. See also Chozo Artifacts, Artifact Temple, Chozo Ghosts, Tallon IV, Phazon.
entries.notes: Removed 'Samus, raised among Chozo, follows it' (no source; WebSearch found only a Gizmodo snippet). Kept the Runic Symbol gate mechanism after checking the Runic Symbol page (symbols occur in identical pairs, and a scanned symbol's counterpart is on a gate that unlocks when all are activated). 'Entrusted One' now leads, with Hatchling and Newborn as alternates; the Chozo Lore page treats the PAL/Trilogy wording as correct. Dropped 'Shining One' as a title. Trimmed to fit the 400-word ceiling. 'Entrusted One', 'Chozo prophecy' and 'Hadar sen olmen' will co-fire with the prime1 prophecy and Raven Beak entries.

entries.content:
Chozo Ghosts, called the Turned in the Chozo Lore, are the spectral remnants of the Chozo of Tallon IV, corrupted by the Great Poison, Phazon. The Chozo's own record describes them as beings utterly corrupted by the Great Poison who still hold to their Chozo forms but whose minds are black with fell intentions: doomed souls in limbo who seek to disrupt the Artifacts that seal the Poison's source. A Holobanner states the cause plainly: The Great Poison corrupts all, even the Chozo. After the meteor strike, as the Chozo faded from the physical world, those who remained suffered in dimensional flux, and the Turned among them were driven mad until they could no longer tell friend from foe.

They haunt places of spiritual significance, above all the Chozo Ruins: the Hall of the Elders, where Samus first met them, and the Sunchamber, where the Artifact of Wild lay. They phase in and out of the visible spectrum, strike quickly and vanish, attacking anything that enters their sacred grounds, yet they can act on the physical world. Fire, ice and electricity pass through them; only the Power Beam and Super Missiles harm them, and the X-Ray Visor is the one reliable way to track them. Space Pirates studying the Ruins took casualties from them and recorded with satisfaction that even ghosts can be destroyed.

Not every spirit was lost. When Meta Ridley shattered the twelve Chozo Totems of the Artifact Temple, twelve Chozo Ghosts appeared in their place, restored the totems in ethereal form and activated the transport into the Impact Crater, opening the way for Samus to destroy the creature Metroid Prime (Metroid Prime). The Chozo Lore had promised that the Chozo's will would persist until the Entrusted One arrived.

For Samus the Turned were a bitter fight. The Chozo who raised her were of Zebes, but the Ghosts wore the shape of her foster people and attacked her in the halls that held the Chozo's last words to her. She destroyed the corrupted and was aided by the sane. See also Phazon, Chozo Artifacts, Artifact Temple, Meta Ridley, Chozo Lore, Tallon IV.
entries.notes: Rated accurate by the fact-check. Replaced 'did not pass on cleanly' with the Lore's own phrasing ('suffer in dimensional flux', 'utterly corrupted'). Dropped the generic key 'the Turned'; 'Turned Chozo' stays. Light trims for length. 'Could no longer tell friend from foe' comes from Wikipedia's character list.

entries.content:
Chozo technology ranks among the most advanced the galaxy has known, and it has outlived its makers. Its hallmarks are longevity, modularity and the fusion of machine with living matter.

The Power Suit is a Chozo invention: modular powered armor that can upload data, accept almost any weapon or modification regardless of origin, and adapt to it at once. Samus's suit was fitted to her by the Chozo of Zebes; per the manga, Mother Brain claimed to have made the Power Suit to support the Chozo's martial strength. By the time of the BSL incident the suit had become so integrated with Samus's body that it could not be removed entirely while she was unconscious (Metroid Fusion). In Chozodia Samus obtained the Legendary Power Suit, a more advanced version of her original suit and the only one able to use the Plasma Beam, Space Jump and Gravity Suit. The Power Beam, Ice Beam, Wave Beam, Plasma Beam, Missile Launcher and Boost Ball are likewise Chozo designs, left for a worthy inheritor in the hands of Chozo Statues; the Chozo of Tallon IV wrote that they left their weapons and armor for the Entrusted One.

The Chozo also built minds and living weapons. On Zebes they created the supercomputer Mother Brain to oversee the planet; on Elysia they built the mechanoid Elysians to maintain SkyTown. Both outlived their makers, and Mother Brain betrayed them. The Thoha bioengineered the Metroids on SR388 to hunt the X Parasites, and on ZDR Raven Beak built robotic Chozo Soldiers to replace his X-infected warriors.

Chozo structures are so old they cannot be dated by ordinary scientific methods. Tallon IV's ruins hold self-lit Holobanners, Radiation Collectors that store solar energy, mechanisms that answer to the Morph Ball, doors keyed to particular beam energies, and the Artifact Temple's Cipher of twelve Artifacts; SkyTown's research pods hover on rocket-like engines.

The Chozo understood what technology costs. Per the manga, the science that gave them long lives compromised their ability to reproduce. On Tallon IV they set advanced technology aside altogether, and they warned younger races such as the Bryyonians to adopt it slowly. Their legacy cuts both ways: the Elysians kept faith, Mother Brain and the Metroids turned on the galaxy, and the Power Suit carried Samus, who wears their greatest work every day. See also Power Suit, Mother Brain, Elysians, Metroids, Chozo Statues, Legendary Power Suit.
entries.notes: Replaced the 'partly organic, absorbed and summoned again' claim with the Fusion fact from Wikipedia: the suit was too integrated with her body to remove entirely while she was unconscious. Replaced 'Mother Brain modified Chozo battlesuit technology' with the manga quote (Mother Brain claimed to have made the Power Suit, Vol 1 Ch 7). Removed the claim about Raven Beak's armor lineage; the robotic Chozo Soldiers are now described accurately. The Legendary Power Suit is called 'a more advanced version of her original suit' (its Metroid Wiki page), not a second suit left by the Chozo. Changed 'carbon-dated' to 'dated by ordinary scientific methods'. Converted the bullet list to prose, removed gameplay framing, and trimmed. Omitted the Power Suit page's unverifiable 'Dryn' developer claim.

result.changelog:
All 10 entries are kept. Each is now 120-400 words, except the main overview, which is 462 words under the allowance for the biggest subjects. The JSON validated (10 entries ok).

Errors fixed:
- History, Metroid creation: only the Thoha created the Metroids; the Thoha and Mawkin later banded together to contain them.
- History, last Chozo: the X did not kill the last known Chozo. The X took Raven Beak's forces, a robot soldier killed Quiet Robe, and Raven Beak fell to Samus.
- Old Bird, afloraltite: the outcome is no longer stated, because the Metroid Wiki Old Bird and Samus Aran pages conflict.
- Old Bird, escape: his unsourced escape during the Pirate invasion was removed.
- Gray Voice: his two verdicts on Mother Brain are now in sequence (Vol 1 Ch 7, then Vol 2 Ch 11).
- Statues: they are no longer described as all sentient or as found on every world. Per the Chozo Statue page, not all are sentient and they stand on the colonized worlds; ZDR was dropped from the list.
- Memories: no longer called the only first-hand account, since Quiet Robe also told Samus. The manga is now described as silent about an SR388 colony, not as contradicting it.

Unverified claims, after one check each:
- Overview, Federation: 'helped found the Federation' was replaced with the manga's 'consolidated their data with the Federation' (Mother Brain page). The DNA is no longer said to be needed to 'bear their armor'; the reason is now the manga's (surviving Zebes).
- Tribes:
  - The revenge vow became 'pressed on to finish the fight'.
  - 'Late in their history' was dropped.
  - Raven Beak's plan to return once the Metroids had wiped out the X was kept. The Raven Beak page states it verbatim.
- Old Bird, training: the fact-check said only Gray Voice trained her, but this was kept. The Samus Aran page says verbatim 'Old Bird and Gray Voice trained her in the ways of the Power Suit.'
- Gray Voice:
  - 'He relented' was removed.
  - 'Serious damage' became 'close to bringing it offline'.
  - 'Samus among them' was removed from the escape.
- Statues:
  - 'Golden' was removed from the fake statue, which is now a Core-X in Sector 1.
  - 'Stone' was removed from the Ruins Test.
  - The vague mutilated statue was replaced by Arachnus smashing the Spring Ball statue.
- Memories:
  - The entry no longer claims Samus found the Memories.
  - 'Sealed in the depths' became 'trapped on the planet'.
- Language:
  - 'Samus follows spoken Chozo' was removed.
  - The paired Runic Symbol gates were kept after checking the Runic Symbol page.
